Schedule C — what to enter and where

Each Schedule C line that will carry an amount, and where on this page the amount comes from. Everything else on Schedule C stays blank. Expenses other than interest go on Schedule D.

This check adds up the numbers the app read and compares the result with the net income printed on the client’s P&L. Every amount is in whole dollars, as NMLS reports them. If they match, nothing was missed or counted twice. If they do not, something on the P&L is missing from, or extra in, the expense list above.

FV7 classification guidance

D510 is income before taxes. Put income tax lines in category K so they are reported on D520.

Schedules C & D — Detailed NMLS filing review

Review field assignments, splits, income, taxes and adjustments before combined XML export.

ExpenseAmountNMLS fieldActions

Use Add expense to enter taxes (D520), extraordinary items (D540) or noncontrolling interest (D560) when applicable. These are separate from gross operating expenses. Amounts represent company totals.

Schedules C & D filing preview

Rounding checks

The three ties NMLS flags when rounding to whole dollars leaves a figure a dollar or two off. Each shows both sides and, when they differ, which line to move. Nothing changes until you click.

Schedule B-350R — Equity rollforward

What to enter on the equity rollforward lines in NMLS. Type last period’s ending equity; the rest comes from the balance sheet and the P&L above.

Lines B350C through B350M (stock issued or repurchased, capital contributions, other comprehensive income, accounting changes, dividends and distributions, noncontrolling interest) are not filled in here. If any apply, enter them in NMLS and reduce B350N by the same amount.

Enter in NMLS

Every NMLS line with an amount, in the order of the NMLS screens. Lines marked “calculated” are added up by NMLS; you do not key them.
